title: With the compiler, do you still need useMemo and memo?

slides.text: Compiler on. Is use memo dead? 🤔
slides.say: With React Compiler on, do you still need use memo and use callback? Mostly not, but there are two cases worth knowing.

slides.text: By default the compiler memoizes based on its own analysis, usually as precisely as you would, or more.
slides.say: By default, the compiler memoizes your code based on its own analysis. In most cases it's as precise as what you'd write, or more.
Case one: precise control. If a memoized value is an effect dependency, use memo can make sure the effect doesn't fire again unless the inputs really change.
Case two: the compiler only memoizes components and hooks, and its cache isn't shared. If many components call a truly expensive function, consider memoizing it outside React.

slides.text: Profile first. Only add manual memoization where you need precise control.
slides.say: But profile first, to check it's really expensive. Then add manual memoization only where you need precise control.
